what_it_measured.text: Preparation, Identification, Molecular Docking Study and Protective Function on HUVECs of Novel ACE Inhibitory Peptides from Protein Hydrolysate of Skipjack Tuna Muscle

dose.text: Following a confluency of 50–60% in the 96-well plates, the cells were treated with 20 µL peptides under designed concentrations (100, 200, and 400 µM) and further cultured for 24 h at 37 ◦ C.

endpoint.text: The sample (10 µL) was eluted at a flow rate of 1.0 mL/min and measured by monitoring the absorbance at 228 nm.
NO and ET-1 production in treated cells were measured by employing human NO and ET-1 assay kit as manufactures’ protocol, separately. 3.8.
The cell viability of TMAP1 and TMAP2 on HUVECs were assessed using the MTT assay on manufacturer’s instructions [65,66].

reported_results.text: SP and VDRYF displayed noticeable ACEi activity, with IC50 values of 0.06 ± 0.01 and 0.28 ± 0.03 mg/mL, respectively.

Furthermore, SP and VDRYF could significantly up-regulate nitric oxide (NO) production and down-regulate endothelin-1 (ET-1) secretion in HUVECs after 24 h treatment, but also abolish the negative effect of 0.5 µM norepinephrine (NE) on the generation of NO and ET-1.

numbers.text: Following a confluency of 50–60% in the 96-well plates, the cells were treated with 20 µL peptides under designed concentrations (100, 200, and 400 µM) and further cultured for 24 h at 37 ◦ C.

SP and VDRYF displayed noticeable ACEi activity, with IC50 values of 0.06 ± 0.01 and 0.28 ± 0.03 mg/mL, respectively.

Furthermore, SP and VDRYF could significantly up-regulate nitric oxide (NO) production and down-regulate endothelin-1 (ET-1) secretion in HUVECs after 24 h treatment, but also abolish the negative effect of 0.5 µM norepinephrine (NE) on the generation of NO and ET-1.
